title: Chest Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset severe tearing/ripping chest pain radiating to the back between the scapulae. Pain is maximal at onset (unlike MI which builds). Exam reveals differential BP between arms (>20mmHg), pulse deficit, new aortic regurgitation murmur. May have neurologic deficits if dissection involves carotid arteries. Risk factors: hypertension (most common), connective tissue disorders (Marfan, Ehlers-Danlos), bicuspid aortic valve, cocaine, pregnancy. CXR shows widened mediastinum (>8cm). CT angiography of chest/abdomen/pelvis is diagnostic. TEE can be done at bedside. Stanford type A (ascending aorta) = SURGICAL EMERGENCY. Stanford type B (descending aorta only) = medical management (BP control). Start IV beta-blocker (esmolol first — lowers dP/dt) then add vasodilator (nitroprusside or nicardipine). Target HR 60 and SBP 100-120. Consult cardiothoracic surgery immediately.
chief_complaint: Severe tearing chest pain radiating to back, maximal at onset
